tasks.how: Read the client brief and the Semantiweb proposal / SOW. Write in one place the topic and its perimeter (e.g. a past study vs a past study), the hypotheses to test (e.g. the client's four shades of satiety), markets and languages, periods, deliverables (deck, exec summary, storyline doc, Talkwalker dashboards) and deadlines.
tasks.tools: Client brief, proposal / SOW, kick-off call notes, Notes the client Account Review & Mapping
tasks.check: Perimeter, markets, languages, periods, deliverables and deadline are written down and agreed with the client.

tasks.how: Set owners, workstreams and a weekly plan (internal brief). Book time in Float, create the Slack channel, plan cover for holidays and the intern workload for the video sample.
tasks.check: Roles, reviewers, milestones and cover are written down and shared.

tasks.how: Create the project folder in the client Drive (01 Set up, 02 Analysis, 03 Excel calculation & query, 04 Presentation) and the extraction workbook with the usual tabs: Brief, Step by Step, Metrics, Queries, Google Trends / Spate.
tasks.tools: Google Drive (the client folder), previous project workbook (the client a past study, a past study)
tasks.check: Folder structure and workbook tabs are ready to fill; old content cleared.

tasks.how: Go through previous the client studies (a past study, a past study, a past study, a past study, F&B) and list what can be reused: queries, ingredient lists, archetypes, benchmarks (High a past study), report structure. Use a past study as the method reference without copying it mechanically.
tasks.tools: ALL FINAL REPORTS folder, previous workbooks and storyline docs
tasks.check: Reuse list with dates; what is reused and what is rebuilt is stated.

tasks.how: Map the trends inside the topic with ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude, then verify with Google, press, reports and a manual TikTok scan. Look at what is happening across markets and in adjacent categories, and log each signal with its source. Output a desk research doc.
tasks.tools: Claude / ChatGPT / Gemini, Google, press, TikTok (manual)
tasks.check: Each signal has a source link; single-market signals are flagged; AI output is checked against real sources.

tasks.how: Export Google search and TikTok hashtag volumes and their evolution from Spate per market. Cluster the keywords into drivers, benefits, pain points, ingredients and formats (as done on proteins). Keep the export for the keyword bubble charts.
tasks.check: Noise removed (brand-led, medical, off-topic keywords); clusters reconcile with the export totals.

tasks.how: From desk research and Spate, propose the structure of the study: buckets / territories (a past study 4 buckets, a past study 4 buckets plus symptoms), ingredients / benefits / occasions (a past study), or client hypotheses (a past study shades). This drives the query list.
tasks.tools: Desk research doc, Spate clusters, client brief
tasks.check: Every territory has a definition and is tied to the brief; overlaps between territories are resolved.
tasks.output: Framework and list of trends / territories to measure

tasks.how: Review the existing topic in the client Talkwalker workspace: read verbatims, spot pollution and gaps, prepare translations per market. Changes need client validation before they go live.
tasks.check: Pollution sources listed; proposed changes validated by the client.

tasks.how: One query per trend, driver, ingredient, benefit, occasion or persona to size, in the Queries tab with one column per language (EN, FR, ES, PT, DE, JP, plus ID on F&B). Hashtags as compacted words, NEAR/n for proximity, NOT instead of AND NOT. For noisy topics, use the topic as a filter inside a broader universe (a past study inside F&B).
tasks.check: Boolean syntax valid (4096 characters, 50 operands); native-language terms for each market; client keywords kept as given when requested.
tasks.output: Draft queries in the Queries tab

tasks.how: Read a random sample of mentions per query and market; add exclusions; tighten proximity where needed; repeat until results are relevant. Back up measurements before rewriting queries.
tasks.check: Precision checked on a sample per market; exclusions noted in the Queries tab.

tasks.task: Define the topic perimeter & draft the main query
tasks.how: Use this phase instead of the topic audit when the topic does not exist in the client Talkwalker workspace (e.g. a past study). Write the main query that extracts the full topic conversation, not a filter query. Start from the desk research, the Spate clusters and the client hypotheses (e.g. the client's four shades of satiety). Write what is in and out of scope, list the keywords and draft the main query in English. Exclude adjacent conversations that pollute the topic (e.g. energy, calories, weight loss for satiety). Use client keywords as given when they ask for it.
tasks.tools: Desk research doc, Spate exports, client brief, Queries tab, building-talkwalker-queries skill
tasks.check: Perimeter written with in / out examples; EN syntax valid (4096 characters, 50 operands); hashtags as compacted words, NEAR/n, NOT instead of AND NOT.
tasks.output: EN main query + keyword list + perimeter note

tasks.task: Validate the main query (if needed, with the client)
tasks.how: Send the EN keyword list and main query to the client with the perimeter note and a few example mentions of what is caught and what is excluded. Translate only after validation.
tasks.check: Client validation received in writing; requested changes applied to the EN version.

tasks.how: Adapt the validated main query into every language of the study (FR, DE, ES, PT, JP, plus any spotlight market agreed in the SOW). Adapt rather than translate word for word: native expressions, local food terms and hashtags. One column per language in the Queries tab.
tasks.tools: Queries tab, building-talkwalker-queries skill, native reviewers
tasks.check: Each language has native terms, not only literal translations; syntax valid in every language.

tasks.task: Test the main query on the tool
tasks.how: Create the topic in Talkwalker as a test. Read a random sample of mentions per language and market, note the noise sources and estimate precision. Check that the volume per market is credible and that the data covers both comparison periods.
tasks.check: Precision checked on a sample per language; noise sources listed; historical coverage confirmed for both periods.

tasks.how: Add exclusions, tighten proximity, remove ambiguous terms, then re-test until precision is acceptable. Log every change and the reason in the Queries tab. If the scope changes, go back to the client.
tasks.check: Precision acceptable in every language; change log up to date.

tasks.task: Create the topic in the client workspace
tasks.how: Create the final topic in the client Talkwalker workspace with the validated main query in every language and the right filters (e.g. Food & Drinks). Document it in the Queries tab and tell the client it is live. From here, measurement and sizing follow the same path as for an existing topic.
tasks.check: Topic live with the validated version in every language; filters documented.
tasks.output: Live topic in the client workspace

tasks.how: For each query and market, pull volume, year-on-year growth (12 vs 12 months, else 6 vs 6), engagement, share of voice, platforms, sentiment, top words and hashtags. Apply the Food & Drinks filter if requested by the client. Check seasonality (24-month curve on a past study). Add Visibrain for TikTok volumes when needed. Fill the Metrics tab.

LESSONS FOR THE NEXT STUDY FOR THIS CLIENT
1. Use a past study as the method reference, but rebuild the structure for each topic instead of copying it (ID cards do not fit every study).
2. Lock queries before measuring: late query rewrites (a past study) force a full rerun of the measurements. Back up data before any change.
3. Give Claude clean inputs (CSV exports, coded sample, framework) and strict rules (no invented numbers, a source per claim, corpus vs TikTok kept apart), as in the F&B brief.
4. Plan client education: explain perimeter, entry points and method early, and get the trend shortlist validated before deep dives.
5. Budget time to rewrite all copy and to check every verbatim against its source before the client sees it.
